hypothesis: If Arizona climate fluctuated with a regular period of almost exactly 150 years over the last 500 years, then century-smoothed ring-width series from Arizona ponderosa pine (yellow pine) will show a dominant, statistically significant spectral peak at about 150 years (140-160 yr), and this peak will recur across independent Arizona chronologies.
pass_criterion: Use Arizona Pinus ponderosa chronologies from the ITRDB that cover at least AD 1400-1900. Smooth each with a 100-year filter, as Douglass did. Then compute a multitaper or Blackman-Tukey power spectrum over AD 1400-1900. The claim passes if, in at least 2/3 of the chronologies (and at least 3 chronologies), the highest spectral peak lies at 140-160 years and exceeds the 95% confidence limit of an AR(1) red-noise null. The claim also needs a pooled regional mean chronology with its main peak at 140-160 years, and the squared coherence of the peak between chronologies must be at least 0.6.
fail_criterion: The claim fails if fewer than half of the qualifying chronologies have their highest peak at 140-160 years, or if the peak in the pooled regional mean does not exceed the AR(1) 95% limit. It also fails if the peak period shifts by more than 25 years between independent sub-periods (AD 1400-1650 versus AD 1650-1900), or if the estimated period's 95% bootstrap interval excludes 150 years. Any of these means no regular 150-year periodicity.
interpretation: Thompson relays Douglass's claim from Flagstaff-area yellow pine (Pinus ponderosa) ring widths. 'Century-smoothed' means a roughly 100-year running mean or low-pass filter applied to ring-width series. 'Regular periodicity' is read as a statistically significant narrow spectral line with a stable period and phase, not just an apparent undulation. 'Climate' is mainly moisture, so ring width is a proxy for precipitation and drought. Modern reinterpretation: use standardized ring-width indices from the ITRDB. Raw widths carry age-related growth trends, and the smoothing itself can create spurious cycles (a Slutsky-Yule effect). A 500-year record contains only about 3.3 cycles of 150 years, so the test has low power and must be judged against a red-noise null. A mismatch in sample depth, or a high-pass filter in the standardization that removes low-frequency variance, would limit the test. Prefer chronologies with conservative detrending (negative exponential or linear).

dataset.name: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB), NOAA NCEI World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI), Paleoclimatology Program
dataset.why_it_fits: The ITRDB holds public ring-width measurement files (.rwl) and standardized chronologies (.crn) with site metadata (state, species code PIPO, latitude and longitude, start and end years). Filter to Arizona Pinus ponderosa sites whose records span at least AD 1400-1900. Use the annual ring-width index and sample depth fields to build the smoothed series, run spectral analysis, and compare against a red-noise null.
